quote: It's just locations of solar panels are the big things. My wife wouldn't wanna see them from the street.
stewart_read: This is a stated aesthetic preference from the wife, not a decision-deferral objection — it does not match protocols.spouse_decision's trigger phrases ('let me ask my wife', decision deferral). It is nonetheless a signal that the wife is an active stakeholder in the design outcome, and the rep never confirmed she'd be included on the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as a routine design-preference detail requiring no further action since it was addressed by design flexibility (south/back roof placement) rather than appointment inclusion.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to note stakeholder signals like this and proactively ask 'will your wife be able to join the call so she can see the panel placement too?' rather than only solving the aesthetic concern technically.

quote: Yep. But we can work up a few designs for you to see, you know, what makes most sense, what what fits your guys' preference and needs, and then kinda let you guys make that decision, of course.
stewart_read: Rep acknowledges 'you guys' will decide together but at no point asks whether the wife will be on the Friday/Saturday appointment itself, leaving the co-owner unconfirmed for the actual review call.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be implicitly assuming the wife will join since the customer referenced her earlier; but nothing on the call confirms this.
coaching_implication: Explicitly confirm co-owner attendance at the point of booking, not just acknowledge joint decision-making in the abstract.

quote: Once we get that bill, we can really finalize it. So I'll just look out for that from you here in in a second, and then we'll plan for Friday. And then I'll just the last bill? We try to look at normally, there's, like, a a bar graph on there with, like, the last since you've been there since September, it should just have till September.
stewart_read: The rep's explanation of the bill's usage graph is disjointed and self-interrupting, suggesting the rep isn't fully confident narrating what the customer should look for on the bill. The customer ultimately supplies the needed data himself.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be a transcription artifact of natural speech rather than a genuine knowledge gap.
coaching_implication: Tighten the bill-explanation script line so it comes out clean and confident — a customer who already has more data than the rep (as happened here) can expose uncertainty in delivery.

quote: So it looks like they had 15.39 kilowatt system, two backup batteries. So it's 38 solar panels is what's on our own dish.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers detailed competitive intel — system size, battery count, panel count from a prior quote — but the rep does not probe further (which company gave this quote, what price, when) before moving straight to 'we'll get ours going for you.'
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have deliberately avoided competitive discussion to stay in setter scope and let the closer handle comparison, which is defensible per setter_scope_discipline.
coaching_implication: At minimum, capture which company provided this quote and note it in the handoff so the closer walks in already knowing the exact competing spec to beat.

quote: Is that not something we can do over the phone?
stewart_read: Customer pushes back on the in-person format after already agreeing to a tentative time, forcing the rep to renegotiate the appointment type mid-call — a sign the original offer wasn't framed clearly as in-person.
alternative_hypothesis: Customer may simply prefer phone regardless of how clearly it was framed, making this a preference statement rather than a clarity failure by the rep.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to state the appointment format explicitly when first offering times ('our specialist will come by in person' or 'this will be a phone call') to avoid a late-call renegotiation.

quote: Yeah. I can do tomorrow at the line.
stewart_read: Customer commits to a specific day for the rescheduled phone appointment, giving the rep a clean close point after the format confusion was resolved.
coaching_implication: This is the moment to lock a specific TIME as well as day, and to run the full button-up (hour block, no-driving/computer, 'is that fair?') — none of which happened here.

quote: Yeah. That's that's perfect. We we're good to go on your end. Perfect.
stewart_read: The call ends without the rep restating the confirmed day/time, without the one-hour block language, without the no-driving/computer instruction, and without the 'is that fair?' handshake — the appointment is left procedurally under-anchored despite being verbally agreed.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may feel the earlier text-based confirmation promise ('shoot me a message there') substitutes for a verbal handshake, but no explicit recap occurred on the call itself.
coaching_implication: Drill the full button-up sequence as a checklist — recap day+time, one-hour block, no-driving/computer instruction, and the fairness handshake — even on calls that feel casually agreed.
